docs.title: code_to_graph Developer Documentation
docs.text:
Welcome to the official developer portal for code_to_graph.

This system converts Python codebases into a graph representation, enriches graph entities with GPT, traces likely runtime workflow, and outputs a professional report.

Best way to use this portal

Start with Quick Start, then read Pipeline Stages and Bevel Integration.

docs.title: What You Get
docs.text:
• Structural Graph

    outputs/raw_graph.json The base graph generated before GPT enrichment.

  • Enriched Graph

    outputs/enriched_graph.json Node-level semantic enrichment with safe fallback behavior.

  • Final Report

    outputs/code_documentation.pdf Professional code documentation for review and submission.

docs.title: Quick Start
docs.text:
Standard modeBevel mode 
pip install -r requirements.txt
python main.py --folder ../book_synthesiser

pip install -r requirements.txt
python main.py --folder ../book_synthesiser --bevel-graph ../bevel-export.json

docs.title: Delivery Checklist
docs.text:
• Build structural graph
  • Enrich graph with GPT/fallback
  • Trace execution workflow
  • Generate code documentation PDF
  • Publish developer docs portal

docs.title: Bevel Integration
docs.text:
This project supports integration with Bevel-Software/code-to-knowledge-graph.

Why this mode exists

It allows you to use Bevel graph extraction while keeping your downstream enrichment and reporting pipeline intact.

docs.title: How It Works
docs.text:
1. Export graph JSON from Bevel.
  2. Pass that JSON via --bevel-graph.
  3. Adapter maps Bevel schema into internal graph model.
  4. Pipeline continues with enrichment, workflow tracing, and report generation.

docs.title: Command
docs.text: python main.py --folder ../book_synthesiser --bevel-graph ../bevel-export.json

docs.title: Adapter Behavior
docs.text:
functions/bevel_adapter.py handles:

  • schema normalization (nodes, edges/connections)
  • relation coercion (calls, imports, defines, inherits_from)
  • symbol-noise filtering

docs.title: AST Overlay in Bevel Mode
docs.text:
pipeline.py overlays AST metadata after Bevel ingest to improve function quality:

  • argument lists
  • return annotations
  • docstrings
  • call edges from parsed code

This is why Bevel mode still produces high-quality function and workflow sections.

docs.title: Data Flow
docs.text:
flowchart TD
  A[Bevel export JSON] --> B[bevel_adapter.py]
  B --> C[Internal graph]
  C --> D[AST metadata overlay]
  D --> E[GPT enrichment]
  E --> F[Workflow trace]
  F --> G[PDF report]

docs.title: Architecture Overview
docs.text:
Core execution flow:

  1. CLI entry (main.py)
  2. Pipeline orchestration (pipeline.py)
  3. Graph generation (standard mode) or graph ingestion (Bevel mode)
  4. GPT enrichment (lang_q/query_engine.py)
  5. Workflow tracing (functions/workflow_builder.py)
  6. PDF generation (functions/pdf_generator.py)
flowchart LR
  A[main.py] --> B[pipeline.py]
  B --> C[Parse or Ingest Graph]
  C --> D[GPT Enrichment]
  D --> E[Workflow Trace]
  E --> F[PDF Report]

docs.title: Key Modules
docs.text:
• main.py: argument parsing, path resolution, run summary printing.
  • pipeline.py: stage orchestration and output emission.
  • code_to_graph/parser.py: AST extraction for classes/functions/imports/calls.
  • code_to_graph/graph_builder.py: graph construction in standard mode.
  • functions/bevel_adapter.py: converts Bevel export to internal graph format.
  • functions/graph_utils.py: graph CRUD/export utilities.
  • lang_q/query_engine.py: GPT calls + robust fallback behavior.
  • functions/pdf_generator.py: report generation and layout.

docs.title: Environment
docs.text:
OpenAI key behavior

Without OPENAI_API_KEY, the pipeline still completes using deterministic fallback descriptions.

Create .env in repository root:

OPENAI_API_KEY=your_key_here

If no key is available, pipeline still runs with fallback descriptions.

docs.title: Run Commands
docs.text:
Standard mode:

python main.py --folder /path/to/python/project

Bevel mode:

python main.py --folder /path/to/python/project --bevel-graph /path/to/bevel-export.json

docs.title: Outputs
docs.text:
All outputs are written under outputs/:

  • raw_graph.json
  • enriched_graph.json
  • code_documentation.pdf

docs.title: Operational Notes
docs.text: Topic Recommendation Target path Always pass project root to --folder Bevel export Use a valid JSON export and pass via --bevel-graph Retry behavior Re-run pipeline after prompt/fallback improvements Deliverables Keep both code PDF and developer docs link

docs.title: Pipeline Stages
docs.text:
pipeline.py runs five explicit stages and prints progress logs.

Execution model

The pipeline is intentionally linear and stage-logged so issues are easy to isolate.

docs.title: Stage 1
docs.text:
• Standard mode: scan files, parse AST, resolve entities, build graph.
  • Bevel mode: load graph from Bevel export JSON.

docs.title: Stage 2
docs.text:
• Standard mode: completed as part of graph build flow.
  • Bevel mode: scan/parse source code and overlay AST metadata onto Bevel nodes.

This overlay improves:

  • function arguments
  • return annotations
  • docstrings
  • same-file call links

docs.title: Stage 3 - Enrichment
docs.text:
lang_q/query_engine.py enriches node metadata with GPT.

  • purpose
  • inputs
  • outputs
  • summary sentence

All GPT calls are protected by try/except, and fallback text is used on failure.

Resilience rule

A single GPT failure must not terminate the whole run.

docs.title: Stage 4 - Workflow Trace
docs.text:
functions/workflow_builder.py builds workflow steps from call edges:

  • identifies likely entry points
  • removes duplicate/redundant steps
  • outputs ordered narrative-friendly sequence

docs.title: Stage 5 - PDF Generation
docs.text:
functions/pdf_generator.py generates a professional report with:

  • Chapter 1: structure overview
  • Chapter 2: function reference
  • Chapter 3: execution workflow
  • Chapter 4: dependency map + architecture snapshot
  • Chapter 5: summary

docs.title: Stage Summary Table
docs.text: Stage Main Owner Output 1 scanner/parser/adapter base graph in memory 2 AST overlay (Bevel mode) richer function metadata 3 query engine enriched graph 4 workflow builder ordered workflow steps 5 pdf generator final report

docs.title: Troubleshooting
docs.text:
First check

Confirm your command path and mode (standard vs --bevel-graph) before deeper debugging.

docs.title: Invalid folder path
docs.text:
Symptom:

  • ValueError: Invalid folder path

Fix:

  • Verify --folder points to a real directory.

docs.title: No Python files found
docs.text:
Symptom:

  • RuntimeError: No Python files found under ...

Fix:

  • Ensure target contains .py files.
  • Point --folder to correct project root.

docs.title: Bevel graph format error
docs.text:
Symptom:

  • Adapter raises schema/format error.

Fix:

  • Re-export valid Bevel JSON.
  • Ensure file path passed to --bevel-graph is correct.

docs.title: Generic function descriptions
docs.text:
Symptom:

  • Function text feels fallback-heavy.

Fix:

  • Set OPENAI_API_KEY in .env.
  • Re-run pipeline.

docs.title: Docs site not opening
docs.text:
Symptom:

  • Local docs link unavailable.

Fix:

mkdocs serve

Open:

  • http://127.0.0.1:8000
